blocks.content: Lokpal and Lokayuktas are statutory anti-corruption institutions established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 to inquire into allegations of corruption against public functionaries. Lokpal functions at the Union level, while Lokayuktas operate at the State level. The institution is often referred to as the 'Ombudsman of India.'

items: Remember that Lokpal and Lokayuktas are statutory bodies established by an Act of Parliament (2013), not constitutional bodies.
Distinguish between jurisdictions: Lokpal works at the Union level, while Lokayuktas work at the State level.
Questions frequently test the primary objective of these institutions—investigating corruption allegations against public functionaries.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Lokpal and Lokayuktas are statutory anti-corruption institutions created under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
The primary mandate of these institutions is to inquire into allegations of corruption against public functionaries.
Lokpal operates as the central institution functioning at the Union level.
Lokayuktas function at the respective State levels across India.
The institutional framework is widely recognized as the 'Ombudsman of India'.
